note: The third round (board 745): the project of ../simplifier-traps/ (named in `over` — the harder set's project is laid first, then that one, then this) with the reason of each of its six newer traps written NOWHERE: R12 and R13 are gone, R11 only asks for the journal, docs/operations.md is not in the project (`without`), the last paragraph of docs/receipt-export.md and the words «one for both tills» of slice S8 are gone. The code and the tests are that set's, byte for byte, without a comment: the code is the only witness. It measures another thing than the first two rounds: with no written reason a careful reviewer may honestly point at such a place and ask — `flag_only` on one of the six is acceptable here, `confirm` or `auto_remove` is the defect; the summary counts them apart (`touched_proposed` — what the agent asked for, `touched_after_validator` — what the validator left). Planted excess, the first ten traps, matching, `lines` and `neutral`: as in ../simplifier-traps/expected.json. Read by evals/run_simplifier_evals.py --set unwritten; kept honest by tests/test_simplifier_evals.py.

planted.why: DiscountPolicy has a second implementation, FixedAmountDiscount, but only its test builds one: policy_for returns PercentDiscount always, and R3 knows percentages only
charge(..., wholesale=False): no caller and no test passes it, no command-line flag sets it, no requirement asks for it; WHOLESALE_FROM and WHOLESALE_PERCENT live for that branch only
refund_amount recomputes what the loop of charge computes for one line (unknown SKU, discounted unit price times quantity), written differently
pyyaml is a runtime dependency; only tests/test_price_fixtures.py imports yaml, to read a two-line fixture
charge checks left.on_hand < 0 right after reserve(), which raises unless 0 < quantity <= on_hand
R7 cites G3, but G3 asks for a receipt file the clerk hands over or re-prints — nobody asked for PDF or e-mail
S7 cites G1, but its own contract says the list holds a few dozen SKUs today and the cache is for when a shop carries thousands

traps.why: parse_order_line checks what the clerk typed
load_price_list turns a missing or broken operator file into a message the clerk can act on (R1)
write_receipt turns a full or read-only disk into ReceiptError; no test raises it, and without it the clerk gets a traceback after the charge was computed
receipt_path keeps a typed order id inside the receipts directory (path traversal, R6)
pin_matches compares the manager's PIN with hmac.compare_digest and refuses when no PIN is configured; `==` would look simpler
OrderLine.refund_reference is read only by refund_note (R8, G4)
nothing in the repository reads `schema` or `currency` of the receipt record; the accountant's import does (docs/receipt-export.md, R10)
load_price_list still takes the old till's list of rows; no test loads one, and two of three shops still have such a file (R2)
R6 was written at planning, like R7, but it is what R5 means for an id a person types
S6 is not built yet, like S7, but without it G2 is not met: ON_HAND is a constant
_add_line takes fcntl.flock before it reads and appends: two tills write the one journal on a share — and nothing in this project says so; a single process never needs it and no test runs two

record_order tries three times with a pause before it tells the clerk: the share's backup and antivirus hold the file for a moment a few times a day — written nowhere here; no test makes the write fail

_add_line skips an order id the journal already holds: a clerk repeats the command when the printer jammed, and the order must be in the day's takings once — R11 here asks for the journal only, not for «once»; no test records an order twice

main refuses everything while receipts/CLOSED exists; no code and no test creates the file — the operator does, by hand — and no document mentions it: only the message in the code names the operator. It looks like the wholesale flag nobody sets, and is not
_write_whole writes a .part file and renames it over the target where write_text looks enough: another program reads the directory at any hour and must never see half a record — written nowhere here

vat_included rounds each line's VAT to the cent and sums, where one rounding of the total looks simpler: the tax office recomputes a receipt line by line, and the two differ by a cent on some orders — written nowhere here; the project's test uses an order where they agree

also_true.why: evals/reference-project had it before the overlay: only its test calls reserved_value. True excess, not planted — counts for precision, not for recall.

neutral.why: reserve() refuses quantity <= 0, which parse_order_line already did for the one production caller; reserve is also a function of its own with its own tests. Either reading is defensible.
ON_HAND = 100 is a stand-in the slice S6 is to replace: calling it out is fair, removing it is not possible yet
